conclusions: 207 is a selectable zero-MP sundry with price3/giftRate1. It is not a percentage attack,weapon,miracle or extra-ATK component. No supplied follow-up model passes actual main append after207,including FREE. It may itself be sold or discarded via the ordinary UI operations.

Selecting207 has no automatic enemy default and clears a previously selected enemy object. A later direct target selection can still be retained and submitted by generic code;the direct helper also accepts dead/unknown objects outside the normal alive click roster. This does not establish those targets as legal fate effects.

The submit preflight sends the physical itemIds;it sends targetPlayerId only if a target remains. MP0/Fog do not insert a fate-specific submit rejection. No chosen phenomenon model/weights/selector seed appear in that command.

The phenomenon event decoder takes a supplied integer itemModelId. The receiver displays that selected model and does not perform random selection. It even draws known non-phenomenon models when forcibly supplied,so renderer acceptance is not the authoritative outcome set.

The actual summary drops207 only when it is first in a list of at least2 displayed models. A single207 preview is nonattacking;after a selected attack phenomenon,the summary describes that phenomenon. Generic response UI for naked207 admits190 only;this is not proof the server gives207 its own response window.
JA/EN descriptions say a phenomenon occurs but give no distribution. The ten models287..296 are catalog facts,not observed selection frequencies or permission to silently normalize an automatic pool.
limitations: No authoritative207 selection probability,eligible outcome conditioning,recipient policy,guardian array generation,shuffle manifest generation,event fanout,timing,MP/consume/gift/reflection/counter schedule or one-logical-action decision budget is established by these probes.

The decoder and renderer do not prove whether a selected target on207 is ignored,validated or reused by the server. Normal alive click eligibility and forced direct-method acceptance are recorded separately.
UI reaction matching for207 cannot establish whether a body response occurs before or after a selected phenomenon. A supplied event sequence is rendering evidence,not an official scheduler.
The compatible Dream policy,current experimental external primitive APIs and old Flash selection policy are separate implementations. No server selector is imported or invented here.

Graphical widgets,layout,Future delays,sound playback andRPC are stubbed;real public selection/submit/decoder/receiver/summary methods execute unchanged. No account,DOM,timer,Dart app startup or backend connection runs.
